subject: MSA + Order Form: output ownership vs. training consent
messages:
From: Julie Park <julie@edgescale.ai>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan@redwood.com>
Cc: Samir Mehta <samir@edgescale.ai>, EdgeScale Legal <legal@edgescale.ai>
Date: Mon, 3 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: MSA + Order Form: output ownership & training consent

Hi Dylan —

Thanks for the draft MSA and order form. Legal flagged two items that are blocking procurement on our side and asked me to escalate:

1) Output ownership: the current language appears to grant Redwood a perpetual license to use customer outputs for productization. EdgeScale needs explicit confirmation that customer-generated outputs (customer prompts + Redwood model responses) remain the customer’s property and cannot be used to train models without opt-in consent.

2) Training / feedback license: the order form lists a generic feedback license. We need either (a) an opt-in checkbox for training consent at the tenant level, or (b) clear timeframe and scope (e.g., anonymized telemetry only, 30-day retention) — otherwise legal will block.

We attached our redlines (EdgeScale_MSA_redline_20260803.pdf) and SOC 2 snapshot for reference. Can we get a proposed path to resolve these so procurement can finish?

Appreciate a quick turnaround — our Q3 rollout depends on this.

Best,
Julie
Business Ops | EdgeScale

Thanks Julie — appreciate the clear notes and the redlines. Looping in Laura and Ben to align legal and product.

Quick read: we definitely don’t want to block your rollout. High-level proposal from our side to unblock for procurement while we finish legal detail:
- Confirm: EdgeScale retains ownership of "Customer Outputs" (as defined) for downstream use. We can add explicit language in Section 7 clarifying that Redwood will not claim title to customer content or outputs.
- Training consent: propose a tenant-level opt-in checkbox on the order form for "Allow Redwood to use de-identified outputs to improve models"; default is OFF. For customers who opt out, we’ll provide a quantifiable telemetry-only fallback (telemetry + anonymized usage stats) that supports service monitoring but not model training.

Ben / Laura — can you weigh in on whether the opt-in checkbox + order form language is sufficient from a legal/contract perspective? Also can we scope the evidence EdgeScale requested (SOC2 snapshot) to a link rather than attachment?

Next steps: I’ll prepare a short mutual action plan and updated order form language if we have alignment. Julie — do you have a procurement deadline this week?

Thanks,
Dylan
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Dylan — thanks for the ping and the suggested path. I reviewed EdgeScale's redline PDF. High-level legal position and suggested redline text below.

1) Ownership / outputs: we can insert explicit language that "Customer retains all right, title, and interest in Customer Data and Customer Outputs." We will also add a carveout that permits Redwood to use aggregated, de-identified telemetry for product analytics but not for model training unless the customer affirmatively opts in on the order form. Suggested clause: "Customer retains ownership of Customer Outputs. Redwood may process and use aggregated, de-identified telemetry solely to operate and improve the Redwood service, provided such data cannot reasonably be re-associated with Customer or an individual. Redwood will not use Customer Data or Customer Outputs to further train or improve base models or proprietary models without explicit written consent."

2) Feedback license: instead of an open-ended feedback assignment, propose a time-bound, narrow license: 12 months for anonymized telemetry used only for service quality improvements, with express exclusions for productization and model retraining. Also document an explicit opt-in mechanism on the order form for any training consent.

3) Evidence requests: we can provide a SOC 2 Type II summary page and a scoped AOC (attestation of control) rather than full reports. Recommend we share a secure link for SOC2 artifacts and require an NDA for deeper material.

If EdgeScale accepts the above, I can produce blackline language for both the MSA and order form today. Two items for product/ops: Karthik, can your team confirm whether an opt-in toggle can be surfaced on the self-serve flow + order form PDF? Laura — from procurement ops, will a checkbox on the order form satisfy their procurement process?

—Ben
Sr. Legal Counsel, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: MSA + Order Form: output ownership & training consent

Ben / Dylan —

Thanks for the quick review. EdgeScale legal likes the high level but pushed back on two points:

1) The phrase "cannot reasonably be re-associated" is a bit soft for procurement — they want a stronger commitment on de-identification standards (NIST/ISO reference), or a prohibition on using outputs for model training regardless of anonymization.

2) The 12-month timebox for telemetry is acceptable only if we get a clear scope of what telemetry includes (request ids, prompt text, token-level traces, usage counters). They want explicit exclusions for prompt text and raw output content.

EdgeScale can accept an opt-in model, but procurement requires the default to be OFF and the checkbox must be on the order form (not buried in console settings). Also they requested an SLA credit if we ever fail to honor training opt-out (they will ask procurement to include a simple remedy).

We can give RD a soft deadline of end-of-week for final redline language. Can you provide the suggested blackline and the SOC2 link by EOD Thursday?

Julie

Subject: Re: MSA + Order Form: output ownership & training consent

Julie — thanks. Summarizing agreed path so procurement can move forward and legal has a single source of truth to redline against: 

1) Ownership: Redwood will add explicit "Customer retains ownership of Customer Outputs" language. Redwood will not use Customer Outputs or prompt text to train models unless the customer opts in via the order form.

2) Training opt-in: we will add a tenant-level checkbox on the order form (default OFF). The checkbox text will be: "I consent to Redwood using de-identified Customer Outputs and aggregated telemetry to improve Redwood models (opt-in)." Any opt-in will be documented in the order form and included in the customer record.

3) Telemetry / timebox: Redwood will permit a 12-month retention/use window for anonymized telemetry for service improvement only. We will explicitly exclude prompt text and raw outputs from telemetry used for model training; telemetry is defined as aggregate usage metrics, latency, error rates, and token counts. We will add NIST 800-188-style de-identification references in the data processing addendum.

4) Evidence: Ben will provide a secure SOC2 summary link (AOC) by Thursday EOD and share the redline blackline for MSA + order form the same day. For any deeper report access, EdgeScale Legal will sign a scoped NDA.

5) Remedy: for the procurement form, we'll draft a simple SLA credit clause for training opt-out violations (minimal, capped) — Ben will include suggested language in the blackline.

Next actions: Ben to send blackline + SOC2 link by Thu EOD. Karthik / Product to confirm checkbox flow and final order form PDF. Laura to log procurement deadline and confirm whether the checkbox on the order form meets their PO system. Julie / EdgeScale to confirm if the above summary is acceptable and we can proceed to finalize.

I'll attach the consolidated action plan and a link to the internal ticket for tracking.

Thanks all — aiming to close this week.

Best,
Dylan
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
